hints.title: Combine inequalities legally
hints.body: You may add inequalities pointing in the same direction. Add a+b<c+d and a+c<b+d.
hints.pitfall: Subtracting or multiplying two inequalities is not automatically valid.

recall.reminder: Track signs and justify each operation used on inequalities.

hints.title: Use the positive information
hints.body: The zeros at the start of the two given chains provide sign information as well as comparisons. Identify exactly which sums have a known sign.
hints.recap: Use the full assumptions, including their sign restrictions.
hints.pitfall: Do not ignore the zeros at the beginning of the supplied chains.
hints.pause: Try combining those sums to test the listed claim about the total.

recall.reminder: All parts of a chained inequality are assumptions you may use.

hints.title: Search for a valid counterexample
hints.body: Try making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> substantially larger than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>, so that you have room to vary the order of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: A counterexample must satisfy both original chains.
hints.pitfall: No claim is disproved by an example that violates a given positivity restriction.
hints.pause: Choose actual numbers, verify both chains, and test the remaining order claim.

recall.reminder: A counterexample must satisfy both original chains.

solution:
Adding a+b<c+d and a+c<b+d gives 2a+b+c<b+c+2d. Cancelling b+c yields a<d, so I is necessary.

From 0<a+b<c+d, both a+b and c+d are positive. Their sum is positive, proving III.

II is not necessary. Set a=1, b=2, c=1, d=4. Then 0<3<5 and 0<2<6, so both assumptions hold, but b<c is false.

I and III only: F.
knowledgePattern: Add inequalities and supply a counterexample to a converse-like inference
